name: Question 3
problem:
Consider the following set of polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t-4,\,{p}_{2}(t)=2-t,\,{p}_{3}(t)=1-t.
$$

Given that the inner product in the vector space ${R}_{1}[t]$ of polynomials of degree at most $1$ in the variable $t$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(1)q(1)+p(2)q(2),
$$

which of the following statements are true?

- ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{3}(t)$ with respect to the given inner product
- ${p}_{2}(t)⊥{p}_{3}(t)$ with respect to the given inner product
- $S={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{3}(t)}$ is an orthogonal set with respect to the given inner product
worked_solution:
Recall that a set of vectors in an inner product space is orthogonal if all vectors in the set are mutually orthogonal with respect to the given inner product. 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{3}(t)⟩ & =⟨2t-4,1-t⟩ \\  & =(2t-4){|}_{1}\cdot (1-t){|}_{1}+(2t-4){|}_{2}\cdot (1-t){|}_{2} \\  & =(2(1)-4)\cdot (1-1)+(2(2)-4)\cdot (1-2) \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{3}(t)$ with respect to the given inner product.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{3}(t)⟩ & =⟨2-t,1-t⟩ \\  & =(2-t){|}_{1}\cdot (1-t){|}_{1}+(2-t){|}_{2}\cdot (1-t){|}_{2} \\  & =(2-1)\cdot (1-1)+(2-2)\cdot (1-2) \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that ${p}_{2}(t)⊥{p}_{3}(t)$ with respect to the given inner product.

- Statement III is false. Let's check if ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{2}(t).$ Computing the inner product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩ & =⟨2t-4,2-t⟩ \\  & =(2t-4){|}_{1}\cdot (2-t){|}_{1}+(2t-4){|}_{2}\cdot (2-t){|}_{2} \\  & =(2(1)-4)\cdot (2-1)+(2(2)-4)\cdot (2-2) \\  & =-2\ne 0,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥̸{p}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the given inner product. So, the set $S$ is *not* an orthogonal set.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

Question 3

Consider the following set of polynomials: p1(t)=2t−4,p2(t)=2−t,p3(t)=1−t. Given that the inner product in the vector space R1[t] of polynomials of degree at most 1 in the variable t is defined as ⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(1)q(1)+p(2)q(2), which of the following statements are true?

  1. p1(t)⊥p3(t) with respect to the given inner product
  2. p2(t)⊥p3(t) with respect to the given inner product
  3. S={p1(t),p2(t),p3(t)} is an orthogonal set with respect to the given inner product
a
None of the statements is true
b
I, II, and III
c
I only
d
II only
e
I and II only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that a set of vectors in an inner product space is orthogonal if all vectors in the set are mutually orthogonal with respect to the given inner product.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, we have ⟨p1(t),p3(t)⟩=⟨2t−4,1−t⟩=(2t−4)|1⋅(1−t)|1+(2t−4)|2⋅(1−t)|2=(2(1)−4)⋅(1−1)+(2(2)−4)⋅(1−2)=0, which means that p1(t)⊥p3(t) with respect to the given inner product.

  • Statement II is true. Indeed, we have ⟨p2(t),p3(t)⟩=⟨2−t,1−t⟩=(2−t)|1⋅(1−t)|1+(2−t)|2⋅(1−t)|2=(2−1)⋅(1−1)+(2−2)⋅(1−2)=0, which means that p2(t)⊥p3(t) with respect to the given inner product.

  • Statement III is false. Let's check if p1(t)⊥p2(t). Computing the inner product, we have ⟨p1(t),p2(t)⟩=⟨2t−4,2−t⟩=(2t−4)|1⋅(2−t)|1+(2t−4)|2⋅(2−t)|2=(2(1)−4)⋅(2−1)+(2(2)−4)⋅(2−2)=−2≠0, which means that p1(t)⊥̸p2(t) with respect to the given inner product. So, the set S is not an orthogonal set.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
